method: Each requirement a catalogue can show gets a score: 100 fully matched, 75/50/25 partially matched (see the definitions), 0 missing capability. A manufacturer's compatibility for one tender item is the average of those scores, and every requirement of the item weighs the same. Unsupported requirements are left out of the average and listed separately. Each requirement is judged against one single product of the manufacturer (the one that suits the item best), so credit is never combined from different products. A manufacturer with no product of the tender's type in its documents, or whose best product fails the requirement that names the type (for example a horizontal pump against a vertical one), scores 0 for that item. An item that no manufacturer's documents can be judged for is not scored at all. The overall compatibility is the average over the scored items, each item weighing the same whatever its quantity. Coverage is the share of the counted requirements for which the documents state something, whether or not it meets the need. Statements that need a person to look (marked review) still count at their score, except those that cannot be compared at all (units that cannot be converted, a tender value that is not a plain number, a statement with no number): they are shown with their flag but left out of the average, so the compatibility rests only on what could be compared.

definitions.fully matched: The manufacturer's document states the requirement, and the stated value meets it (score 100).
definitions.partially matched: The document says something relevant but not enough to be sure: the value is higher than asked (75), applies only under a condition or to a product that is not named (75), is the same kind of thing but not the grade or number asked for (50), meets the need only if a unit such as PN is read the other way (50), or cannot be compared at all, such as units that cannot be converted or a statement with no number (25). These are flagged for review, and the ones that cannot be compared are shown but left out of the compatibility.
definitions.missing capability: A catalogue could show this requirement and at least one manufacturer's documents speak to it, but this manufacturer's documents state nothing about it, or state something that does not meet it (score 0).
definitions.unsupported requirement: A requirement about which no manufacturer can be judged from catalogues: it needs a certificate or other document, it only identifies the item or where it is used, or none of the collected documents covers it. It is not scored and not held against anyone; it is listed so the bid manager can confirm it with the manufacturer.
